questions.stem: A rectangle has length $8.2\,\text{cm}$ and width $3.5\,\text{cm}$, both measured to $1$ decimal place. What is the upper bound of the area?
questions.explanation: For the maximum area, use the upper bound of both measurements. Upper bound of length $= 8.25$, upper bound of width $= 3.55$. Maximum area $= 8.25 \times 3.55 = 29.2875\,\text{cm}^2$.

questions.stem: To find the upper bound of $\frac{a}{b}$, you should use:

options.text: Upper bound of $a$ divided by upper bound of $b$
Lower bound of $a$ divided by lower bound of $b$
Upper bound of $a$ divided by lower bound of $b$
Lower bound of $a$ divided by upper bound of $b$

questions.explanation: To maximise a fraction, make the numerator as large as possible and the denominator as small as possible. So use the upper bound of $a$ and the lower bound of $b$.

questions.stem: A distance is $100\,\text{m}$ to the nearest $10\,\text{m}$. A time is $12.5\,\text{s}$ to $3$ significant figures. What is the lower bound of speed $\left(\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}\right)$?
questions.explanation: For the minimum speed, use the smallest distance and the largest time. Lower bound of distance $= 95\,\text{m}$, upper bound of time $= 12.55\,\text{s}$. Minimum speed $= \frac{95}{12.55}$.
